items.title: Section: The Five Loci Where Yogic Practice Is Established

items.zh: 於四種處，以四因緣正尋求已，復於五處如應安立。云何五處？一、護養定資糧處，二、遠離處，三、心一境性處，四、障清淨處，五、修作意處。
items.en: Having rightly sought out the four matters through the four means, one next establishes yogic practice, as is fitting, at five loci. What are the five loci? First, the locus of safeguarding the provisions for concentration. Second, the locus of seclusion. Third, the locus of one-pointedness of mind. Fourth, the locus of purifying obstructions. Fifth, the locus of cultivating mental engagement.

items.title: Safeguarding the Provisions for Concentration: Precepts as the First Example

items.zh: 云何護養定資糧？謂若成就戒律儀者，即於是處為令不退，住不放逸；如佛所誡、如佛所許，圓滿戒蘊學處差別，精進修行，常無懈廢。如是能於己所證得尸羅相應學道無退，亦能證得先所未證尸羅相應殊勝學道。
items.en: What is safeguarding the provisions for concentration? That is, if he has already accomplished the moral discipline of restraint, then, right at this point, in order to prevent his falling back from it, he abides in non-heedlessness; in accordance with what the Buddha has prohibited and what the Buddha has permitted, he perfects the various precepts making up the aggregate of moral discipline, cultivating them diligently and without ever slackening or abandoning them. In this way he neither falls back from the path already realised in conjunction with moral discipline, nor fails to realise the superior path in conjunction with moral discipline not yet realised.

items.zh: 如說成就戒律儀，如是成就根律儀、於食知量、初夜後夜覺寤瑜伽、正知而住，如是乃至成就所有沙門莊嚴，隨所獲得資糧所攝善法差別，皆能防護令不退失。於後勝進善法差別，為速圓滿，為如所說無增無減平等現行，發生樂欲，增上欣慕，恒常安住勇猛精進。是名護養定資糧。
items.en: As said of accomplishing the moral discipline of restraint, so too with accomplishing restraint of the faculties, moderation in eating, the yoga of wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night, and abiding with clear comprehension — and so on up through accomplishing every ornament of a true renunciant: whatever wholesome states belonging to the provisions have been attained, all of them are safeguarded so that they do not decline. As for the further, more advanced wholesome states still to come, in order to swiftly perfect them, and to manifest them evenly, neither adding to nor subtracting from what has been taught, one gives rise to the wish for them, increasingly cherishes and longs for them, and constantly abides in courageous diligence. This is called safeguarding the provisions for concentration.

items.title: Section: The Locus of Seclusion Opens

items.zh: 如是遠離順退分法，修習能順勝分法時，樂住遠離。
items.en: Having thus abandoned the states conducive to decline, at the time of cultivating states conducive to what is superior, one takes joy in dwelling in seclusion.

items.zh: 云何遠離？謂處所圓滿、威儀圓滿、遠離圓滿，是名遠離。
items.en: What is seclusion? That is, perfection of place, perfection of deportment, and perfection of seclusion — this is called seclusion.

items.title: Perfection of Place: Where a Practitioner May Dwell

items.zh: 謂或阿練若、或林樹下、或空閑室。山谷、巖穴、稻秆積等，名空閑室。大樹林中，名林樹下。空逈、塚間、邊際臥坐，名阿練若。當知如是山谷、巖穴、稻秆積等，大樹林中，空逈、塚間、邊際臥坐，或阿練若、或林樹下、或空閑室，總名處所。
items.en: That is, either a forest hermitage, or beneath a grove of trees, or an unoccupied dwelling. Mountain valleys, rocky caves, heaps of rice-straw, and the like are called an unoccupied dwelling. The midst of a great forest is called beneath a grove of trees. Open wilderness, a charnel ground, or a bare minimum of seating and bedding are called a forest hermitage. Know that all of these — mountain valleys, rocky caves, heaps of rice-straw, the midst of a great forest, open wilderness, a charnel ground, bare minimum seating and bedding, whether a forest hermitage, beneath a grove of trees, or an unoccupied dwelling — are together called "a place."

items.title: Section: The Five Qualities of a Perfect Place

items.zh: 謂若處所，從本已來形相端嚴，眾所憙見，清淨無穢；園林池沼悉皆具足，清虛可樂；地無高下，處無毒刺，亦無眾多甎石瓦礫；能令見者心生清淨，樂住其中修斷加行；心悅、心喜，任持於斷。是名第一處所圓滿。
items.en: First: a place whose form has always been dignified and pleasing to behold, pure and free of filth; complete with gardens, groves, and ponds, clear, open, and delightful; its ground level, free of thorns and poisonous growths, and free of brick, stone, and rubble; able to make anyone who sees it feel purified at heart and glad to dwell there applying effort towards severing affliction — the mind delighted, the mind joyful, sustaining that severing. This is the first perfection of place.

items.zh: 又若處所，晝無憒鬧，夜少音聲，亦少蚊虻、風日、蛇蠍諸惡毒觸。是名第二處所圓滿。
items.en: Second: a place free of clamour by day, with little sound by night, and with few mosquitoes and gadflies, little harsh wind or sun, and little contact with snakes, scorpions, or other venomous, harmful creatures. This is the second perfection of place.

items.zh: 又若處所，無惡師子、虎、豹、豺、狼、怨敵、盜賊、人非人等諸恐怖事；於是處所，身意泰然，都無疑慮，安樂而住。是名第三處所圓滿。
items.en: Third: a place without fierce lions, tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, hostile enemies, bandits, or menacing humans and non-humans — a place where body and mind are at ease, entirely without apprehension, dwelling there in peace and happiness. This is the third perfection of place.

items.zh: 又若處所，隨順身命眾具易得，求衣服等不甚艱難，飲食支持無所匱乏。是名第四處所圓滿。
items.en: Fourth: a place where the various necessities that sustain body and life are easily obtained, where seeking clothing and the like is not too difficult, and where the sustenance of food and drink is never lacking. This is the fourth perfection of place.

items.zh: 又若處所，有善知識之所攝受，及諸有智同梵行者之所居止；未開曉處能正開曉，已開曉處更令明淨；甚深句義以慧通達，善巧方便殷勤開示，能令智見速得清淨。是名第五處所圓滿。
items.en: Fifth: a place where one is cared for by a good spiritual friend, and where wise fellow practitioners of the pure life also dwell; where what is not yet understood can be correctly clarified, and what is already understood can be made yet more luminous and pure; where profound meanings are penetrated with wisdom, taught tirelessly and skilfully, so that one's wisdom and insight are swiftly purified. This is the fifth perfection of place.

items.title: Perfection of Deportment: The Daily Rhythm and Cross-Legged Sitting's Five Reasons

items.zh: 謂於晝分經行、宴坐；於初夜分亦復如是；於中夜分右脇而臥；於後夜分疾疾還起，經行、宴坐。即於如是圓滿臥具，諸佛所許大小繩床、草葉座等結加趺坐，乃至廣說。
items.en: That is, during the day one paces in walking meditation and sits in stillness; during the first watch of the night one does likewise; during the middle watch one lies down on the right side; and during the last watch one rises quickly and again paces and sits in stillness. Upon such proper bedding — rope-beds large or small, or grass-and-leaf seats permitted by the buddhas — one sits cross-legged, and so on at length.

items.zh: 何因緣故結加趺坐？謂正觀見五因緣故。一、由身攝斂速發輕安。如是威儀順生輕安最為勝故。二、由此宴坐能經久時。如是威儀不極令身速疲倦故。三、由此宴坐是不共法。如是威儀外道他論皆無有故。四、由此宴坐形相端嚴。如是威儀令他見已極信敬故。五、由此宴坐佛佛弟子共所開許。如是威儀一切賢聖同稱讚故。正觀如是五種因緣，是故應當結加趺坐。
items.en: For what reason does one sit cross-legged? That is, because one rightly observes five reasons. First, because the body being drawn together swiftly gives rise to pliancy. Second, because sitting thus one can endure for a long time. Third, because this sitting posture is a teaching not shared with outside paths. Fourth, because this sitting posture's form is dignified and proper. Fifth, because this sitting posture is what the buddhas and their disciples have, together, permitted. Rightly observing these five reasons, one should therefore sit cross-legged.

blocks.text: The teacher now establishes the student's practice in five areas. Today, the first two: safeguarding the provisions, and seclusion, including the five qualities of a good place to practise.
Safeguarding the provisions for concentration; seclusion; one-pointedness of mind; purifying the obstructions; cultivating attention.

If the student already keeps the precepts, the teacher helps protect and nourish them. Venerable Miào Jìng: 護 is protecting, 養 is nurturing. The teacher explains what the Buddha prohibited and permitted, "neither adding to nor subtracting from what has been taught". Likewise for sense restraint, moderation in eating, wakefulness.
"Perfection of place, perfection of deportment, and perfection of seclusion."
A forest hermitage, beneath trees, an empty dwelling: "mountain valleys, rocky caves, heaps of rice straw".

subs.head: Five qualities of a good place

items: Pleasant to see, clean, with gardens, groves, and ponds.
Quiet by day and night; "few mosquitoes and gadflies, little harsh wind or sun".
Safe: no wild beasts, enemies, or bandits; "where body and mind are at ease".
"Where one is cared for by a good spiritual friend, and wise fellow practitioners also dwell; where what is not understood can be asked."

blocks.text: By day, walking and sitting; first watch, the same; middle watch, sleep on the right side; last watch, rise and practise. Why sit cross-legged? Five reasons: it quickly brings pliancy; it can be held long; it is not shared with other traditions; its form is dignified and proper; and the Buddhas and their disciples have permitted it. Venerable Miào Jìng: outside paths sit in other postures.

quiz.q: What are the five loci, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say safeguarding the provisions is?
options: safeguarding, seclusion, one-pointedness, purification, engagement; protecting and nurturing the provisions — the two-path provisions
quiz.why: "First, the locus of safeguarding the provisions for concentration. Second, seclusion. Third, one-pointedness of mind. Fourth, purifying obstructions. Fifth, cultivating mental engagement." Master Cháng Bǎi: protecting and nurturing the provisions for concentration — the two-path provisions described in this treatise.

quiz.q: How do the masters break down the two characters of 護養 (safeguarding)?
options: both: 護 protects from loss, 養 nurtures growth; Cháng Bǎi adds strengthening the provisions
quiz.why: "This is called safeguarding the provisions for concentration." Venerable Miào Jìng: 護 is protecting, 養 is nurturing — within our discriminating mind, calm and insight must be nurtured continually. Master Cháng Bǎi: not losing them is protection; nurturing means increasing — growing merit and strengthening the provisions.

quiz.q: "Neither adding to nor subtracting from what has been taught." What does Venerable Miào Jìng warn?
options: don't cleverly add — do as the Buddha said
quiz.why: "To manifest them evenly, neither adding to nor subtracting from what has been taught." Venerable Miào Jìng: don't be clever and add to it — if the Buddha said so and you feel it's not enough and want more, don't!

quiz.q: Seclusion includes perfection of place and more. What does Venerable Miào Jìng remind practitioners to watch?
options: the wider environment matters too — resolve alone isn't enough
quiz.why: "What is seclusion? That is, perfection of place, perfection of deportment, and perfection of seclusion." Venerable Miào Jìng: you must also attend to the wider environment — resolving to practise is not enough.

quiz.q: The second quality: "few mosquitoes, 風日." The English says "little harsh wind or sun." How do the lectures read 風日?
options: Miào Jìng: animals chasing each other, admitting uncertainty; Cháng Bǎi's second reading: animals luring mates
quiz.why: "With few mosquitoes and gadflies, little harsh wind or sun." Venerable Miào Jìng: 風日 means animals chasing one another — "that's my reading; I haven't read much, so I'm not sure." Master Cháng Bǎi: animals luring mates is also called 風 — when birds and beasts chase each other. The English takes only the literal "wind and sun."

quiz.q: The first quality ends "the mind delighted, the mind joyful." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: delight is in the place; joy is anticipating future attainment there
quiz.why: "The mind delighted, the mind joyful, sustaining that severing. This is the first perfection of place." Venerable Miào Jìng: delight is gladness about the place; joy is anticipating that one will achieve something here.

quiz.q: The third reason for cross-legged sitting: "not shared with outside paths." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: outside paths and non-Buddhist texts don't teach this posture
quiz.why: "Third, because this sitting posture is a teaching not shared with outside paths." Venerable Miào Jìng: outside paths and other treatises — books outside the Buddha's teaching — do not describe this posture, so it is "not shared."
